subject: How to simulate drought for a given location

messages.author: f9f1c443eac95d14
messages.subject: How to simulate drought for a given location
parts:
Hi everyone,
Is there a way to simulate drought with the micro_global function for a given location?

There are many definitions of drought in the literature. For example, when there is a prolonged time with less than average precipitation, or an increase in vapor pressure deficit (VPD). I was thinking of changing the VPD given the non-standard lack of rainfall for a long period is a bit subjective. Some use time and others use below-average rainfall.

I had a look at the micro_global function on GitHub (https://github.com/mrke/NicheMapR/blob/master/R/micro_global.R) but there was no option for VPD. Any advice or recommendations that could help simulate drought?

Much appreciated,
Nicholas

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: How to simulate drought for a given location
parts:
Hi Nicholas,

Reducing the rainfall would seem to be the most obvious way to impose a drought though. It really depends on what process you're trying to modify for what species.

Is it altering the water intake? That would then require a prediction of food water content and the possibility of drinking from rain. You could use the plantgro function to simulate plant water content as a function of soil water potential.

Is it altering water loss? That would be driven by atmospheric water content, i.e. vapour pressure/humidity.

To alter the vapour pressure, you'd need to modify the relative humidity coming from the global_climate.nc file that is used as input. You'd have to convert it first to vapour pressure with the WETAIR function, drop it by the factor you're after, and then convert it back to relative humidity to then be passed to the microclimate model. That would require modifying the micro_global function.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: How to simulate drought for a given location
parts:
Hi Mike,
I had help from Urtzi, and we made a modified version of micro_global() called micro_glboal_drought() in the attached email with the goal of simulating drought by changing either changing 1) vapour pressure and 2) relative humidity (RH). Urtzi applied a "drought factor" (new function parameter 'dfact') to the vapour pressure and then converted it back to RH (lines 492-502). In the second version (micro_global_drought2), he directly applied the drought factor to RH (lines 1554-1558). And results are exactly the same (red and blue lines in plots below). Soooo, we are not entirely convinced that I did correctly the RH -> VP -> RH conversions... any insights to why this might be?

Note, drought factor 'dfact' with a value of 0.2 means 20% of the original RH or VP.


* Blue and red lines overlapped. 

Cheers,
Niky

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: How to simulate drought for a given location
parts:
Hi Niky (and Urtzi),

Sorry, I led you astray there. If there are no changes to the temperature, then you can indeed just cut the relative humidity down by a factor and that is the same as computing the vapour pressure from temperature and humidity, adjusting vapour pressure by a factor, and then recomputing the relative humidity. Note that your adjustment used the maximum temperature to compute the maximum relative humidity, but it should really have been the minimum temperature because max humidity for the same vapour pressure will happen at the minimum temperature. But because you didn't change the temperature at all, it didn't matter. If you are wanting to change BOTH temperature and humidity, you should definitely do it via vapour pressure.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: How to simulate drought for a given location
parts:
Hi Mike,

Thanks a lot for the response. I have tried using min temperature for max humidity (and vice versa for min humidity) using this code:

# correct for drought factor
    # first for min RH
    VPMINNsat <- WETAIR(db = TMAXX, rh = 100)$esat # compute saturation vap pressure
    VPMINN <- WETAIR(db = TMAXX, rh = RHMINN)$e # compute vap pressure
    VPMINNd <- VPMINN * dfact # drop it by the factor you're after
    RHMINN <- (VPMINNd / VPMINNsat) * 100 # convert back to RH
    # then for max RH
    VPMAXXsat <- WETAIR(db = TMINN, rh = 100)$esat
    VPMAXX <- WETAIR(db = TMINN, rh = RHMAXX)$e
    VPMAXXd <- VPMAXX * dfact
    RHMAXX <- (VPMAXXd / VPMAXXsat) * 100

However, I still get the same results as when I just cut the RH by the same factor... What am I doing wrong?

Thank you so much in advance!

All the best,
Urtzi

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: How to simulate drought for a given location
parts:
Hi Urtzi,

If you're changing the air temperature but have no data on the vapour pressure and whether it is changing, and want to keep it the same, you need to adjust the relative humidity using the method in your code. Because if you just change the temperature and leave the relative humidity as is, you are imposing a change on the vapour pressure implicitly. Make sense? So the behaviour you saw was correct - cutting the vapour pressure down by a fixed fraction is the same as cutting the RH. I was wrong initially when I said you had to do it via the vapour pressure only.

All the best,
Mike
